--- original

@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8180'
+title: State what postingTo does not carry, and which correlation the journal keeps
+---
+## What
+
+`ToolContext.mount(_:op:as:postingTo:)` (card ^bbbkas1) has a documentation comment
+that is false in a way a reader cannot detect. Two corrections, both measured by the
+consumer against `d576a72`.
+
+### 1. The sink does not carry a swept terminal
+
+The comment says the caller's sink observes every event the run produces. It does not.
+`close()` sweeps a background run through the MAILBOX, and a mailbox-originated
+terminal never passes through the mount's sink at all.
+
+Measured, one background shell run, after `close()`:
+
+```
+run's own token = 01M1C1R4H4VWK7MJTKYVP322JQ
+mounting run    = 01M1C1R4H3G4WSP07XB1EG5V2H
+
+caller sink : kinds=[.progress]   correlations=[01M1C1R4H4VWK7MJTKYVP322JQ]
+journal     : kinds=[.completed]  correlations=[01M1C1R4H4VWK7MJTKYVP322JQ]
+```
+
+The `.progress` event reached the sink on the run's own token, so `postingTo:` works
+and survives backgrounding. The terminal went only to the journal.
+
+The behaviour is probably correct: a mailbox-originated event is not the run posting
+something of its own. This card does not change it. It makes the comment say what is
+true — the sink carries what the RUN posts, and a swept terminal is read from the
+journal.
+
+### 2. The journal's correlation depends on which overload mounted the run
+
+Neither the consumer nor this package predicted this, and it is a real consequence of
+`postingTo:`:
+
+| mounted with | journal shows |
+|---|---|
+| `mount(_:op:as:)` | the MOUNTING run's token — `MountedRunUpstreamSink` re-stamps |
+| `mount(_:op:as:postingTo:)` | the run's OWN token — no re-stamping layer in the path |
+
+So the same journal read gives a different correlation depending on a choice made at
+the mount site. That is defensible, and it is invisible. Say it in both doc comments.
+
+## What to do
+
+Correct the two doc comments in
+`Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Hosting/ToolContext.swift`. No behaviour changes and
+no signature changes.
+
+- The `postingTo:` comment must state that the sink carries the events the RUN posts,
+  and must name the swept terminal as the case it does not carry, with the journal as
+  where that is read.
+- Both comments must state which correlation the JOURNAL carries under that overload,
+  because the two answers differ and the difference is invisible at the call site.
+
+Write it so a reader choosing between the overloads can predict what each will show
+them, in both the sink and the journal, without running anything. That is the whole
+point: the consumer got this matrix wrong twice today in opposite directions, and so
+did this package.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The `postingTo:` comment says the sink carries what the run posts, and names the
+      swept terminal as the exception.
+- [ ] Both comments state which correlation the journal keeps under that overload.
+- [ ] No signature and no behaviour changes. The public surface stays at 652.
+- [ ] A reader can predict, from the comments alone, what each overload shows in the
+      sink and in the journal.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] A test that a swept background run's terminal does NOT reach the caller's sink,
+      so the documented exception is enforced rather than only described. If that
+      cannot be built here — `close()` sweeping needs a session the unit suite may not
+      assemble — say so plainly on the card and leave the comment as the record.
+- [ ] Run `swift test`. All tests pass.
+
+## Note
+
+Found by the downstream consumer, measured, on the day the API shipped. It reported it
+as "not asking you to change this" and was right about the behaviour; the defect is
+that this package's own words did not match it. #router #api #docs
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m1cy96hvbxaa727h6dnnyqse
+  text: |-
+    ### Research — verified against the source
+
+    I read `SessionMailbox.sweep()`, `RoutedSessionActor.close()`, `SessionOutbox.journalWithoutStaging(event:)`, `ToolRun`/`RunEventFunnel`, `BackgroundToolRunner.launch(arguments:)`, `ToolMounting.makeWrapped(...)`, and both `mount` overloads. The card is correct about the defect. It is not complete about the journal.
+
+    **What the sink carries.** `ToolRun` builds a `RunEventFunnel(upstream: sink, ...)` and gives the run a `ToolContext` whose sink IS that funnel. So every event the run posts — `post(_:)`, `progress(_:)`, `elicit(_:)` — reaches `sink` stamped with the run's own `tool`, `op`, and `completionToken`. A run that ends on its own also reaches `sink`: `ToolRun.settle(arguments:)` builds the terminal and calls `funnel.settleRun(with:)`, which forwards it upstream.
+
+    **What the sink does not carry.** `close()` calls `mailbox.sweep()`. For a run still tracked, `sweep()` runs the run's canceler and, when no natural terminal has been retained, SYNTHESIZES a terminal itself: `OperationEvent(tool: run.tool, op: run.op, correlationID: token, kind: .completed, detail: run.latestProgressDetail ?? "", outcome: <canceler's outcome>)`. That event is built inside the mailbox. It never passes the funnel, so it never reaches `sink`. `close()` then writes it with `outbox.journalWithoutStaging(event:)` — straight to the session journal.
+
+    **Correction to the card's table.** The card says the journal's correlation depends only on the overload. That is true for what the RUN posts, but not for the swept terminal:
+
+    | | what the run posts | a swept terminal |
+    |---|---|---|
+    | `mount(_:op:as:)` | journal keeps the MOUNTING run's token (`MountedRunUpstreamSink` -> `post(_:)` re-stamps) | journal keeps the mounted run's OWN token |
+    | `mount(_:op:as:postingTo:)` | goes to `sink` only, on the run's own token; it reaches the journal only if `sink` itself forwards there | journal keeps the run's OWN token |
+
+    The swept terminal is the same under both overloads, because `sweep()` reads what `mailbox.track(...)` registered, and `BackgroundToolRunner.launch(arguments:)` registers the mounted run's own tool, op, and completion token. Both overloads share one mailbox: `ToolMounting.makeWrapped(tool:inheriting:sink:...)` passes `context.mailbox` through.
+
+    Two more facts the docs should carry:
+    - With `postingTo:` and a sink of the caller's own, the run's live events never reach the journal at all. That is why the consumer measured `sink kinds=[.progress]` and `journal kinds=[.completed]` with no overlap.
+    - Cancelling a `.swiftTask` run is cooperative, so a swept run can still finish afterwards and post its OWN terminal to `sink`, with a different outcome from the journaled one. `close()`'s own doc comment already records that, and `claimJournalWrite(for:)` keeps the journal at one terminal per run.

+    ### Implementation notes
+
+    **Doc comments.** Three blocks in `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Hosting/ToolContext.swift`:
+
+    1. `mount(_:op:as:)` — removed the false clause "and it never reaches the outbox", and added two paragraphs: which correlation the journal keeps for posted events (THIS run's token), and the swept-terminal exception (the mounted run's own token, written by `close()` straight to the journal).
+    2. `mount(_:op:as:postingTo:)` — replaced the clause "so `sink` keeps taking that run's progress events and then its terminal". It now states what `sink` carries, what it does not carry (the swept terminal, with the journal as where to read it), which correlation the journal keeps, and the cooperative-cancellation tail.
+    3. `MountedRunUpstreamSink` — the type's own doc said "forwarding every event the run produces" and "the mounted run's own completion token stays on the run plane". Corrected to "every event the run POSTS", with a new paragraph saying a swept terminal takes no route through the sink at all. A finding shows one example of a cause; this was the same false claim in the same file.
+
+    Two extra facts I found while checking the claims, and wrote into the `postingTo:` comment because the old wording would otherwise still promise more than the code delivers:
+
+    - `RunEventFunnel.settleRun(with:)` delivers a terminal only when `hasDeliveredAnyEvent || outcome != .succeeded`. So a run-to-completion run that posted nothing of its own and then succeeded posts NO terminal. A binding-only mount (`ContextBindingTool`) synthesizes no events at all. A background mount always posts the launch envelope as `.progress` first, so it always delivers.
+    - Cancelling a `.swiftTask` run is cooperative, so a swept run can still finish and post its own terminal to `sink` with a different outcome from the journaled one.
+
+    **Test.** `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/MountedRunSweptTerminalTests.swift`, one test.
+
+    **A dead end worth recording, so the next agent does not repeat it.** My first attempt drove the mount from a real turn, through `ScriptedSessionFixture`, and held the mounted background run past the turn. It hangs, and it will hang for anyone who tries it. `RoutedSessionActor.respond(to:maxTokens:)` runs a RUN-PLANE DRAIN after the model call: `settleBackgroundRuns(cancellationsBefore:)` waits for every run tracked on the mailbox to settle, with a deadline of `ToolContext.deadlineSecondsCeiling` (one day). A run held on a gate never settles, so the turn never returns and `close()` is never reached. The `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))` trait turned that into a 64-second failure rather than a hung suite.
+
+    The working shape runs no turn at all. It vends a real session over `UndrivenLanguageModelContainer`, hand-builds the mounting `ToolContext` over that session's own `mailbox` and `outbox` (`@testable` reaches the internal initializer), mounts `MountFixtures.GatedTool` as background with `postingTo:` a `MountFixtures.RecordingSink`, and calls `close()` with the gate still shut. `close()` journals swept terminals whether or not the session ever generated — `SessionMailboxTests` already relies on that.
+
+    The test asserts, in order: the sink holds the launch `.progress` under the run's own token (the liveness proof); the sink holds NO `.completed`; the journal holds exactly one `.completed`, under the run's own token, with outcome `.cancelled`; the journal holds no `.progress`; and, after the gate opens, the run posts its own `.completed` to the sink with outcome `.succeeded`.
+
+    **Falsification check.** I inverted the central assertion to `#expect(atClose.contains { $0.kind == .completed })` and re-ran. It failed on that one line and on nothing else, so the assertion is live and the other assertions are not propping it up. Then I restored it.
+
+    **Public surface.** The Sources diff is `///` text only. It adds, removes, and re-signs no declaration, so the surface count cannot have moved. I did not independently count 652.
